contradicted: Two things this dispatch's own text asserted turned out imprecise, both worth recording rather than smoothing over (DEV_PROCESS 3.2/3.2a). First, defect 3's premise names the binding question as 'is PLATFORM_INTERNAL_API_KEY bound to tenant_id=2' -- at source, the KEY itself is never bound to any tenant at all (it is one bearer secret gating all 12 /api/platform/* routes uniformly, confirmed via requirePlatformInternalKey's implementation and commit d2d3648's exemption of /platform from session-auth); tenant resolution is a per-ROUTE implementation choice downstream of the key, and it is not one answer but three different mechanisms across the 12 routes -- see defect3.answer below. Second, this dispatch's checkpoint-path section warns that lanes have written into the property seat's worktree by mistake; the mirror-image nearly happened here for a different reason -- a pre-existing empty local branch named g126-tenant-isolation sat in the RAW P:/smartcity-dashboards checkout (not a registered worktree, created 2026-09-14 13:49, zero unique commits), and only discovering the DEDICATED registered worktree at P:/smartcity-dashboards-worktrees/g126-tenant-isolation (via a 'branch already used by worktree' error, not by knowing to look) prevented defect 2's work from landing in the wrong checkout.
leave_behind: Defect 2's honest residual, stated in the PR and the mygov-permits.mjs header rather than worked around: smartcity-os's dbPermitToApi drops the row's own tenantId from its response shape entirely, so no per-RECORD verification is possible from smartcity-dashboards' side today -- only a per-PACK guard (assertVerifiedMygovTenant) was buildable without touching the no-touch repo or inventing a field. Closing the upstream gap for real needs dbPermitToApi to surface tenantId (or a public-safe derived city identifier); that is smartcity-os feature work, out of this mission's authorization.

Defect 3's finding is a report, not a fix, by explicit mission design (ABSOLUTE NO-TOUCH, authorization scoped to reading and reporting). The concrete, nameable risk left standing: /api/platform/property-intel/summary resolves its tenant via the bare DEFAULT_TENANT_ID literal (=2), which already changed once (0e5c41e, 1->2, for an unrelated manager-load fix) and feeds a real SQL tenant_id filter (getPropertySummary -> getPropertyPermits/getPropertyViolations/getPropertyInspections, each `WHERE tenant_id = $1`). A second unrelated bump, or a tenant renumbering, would silently serve a different tenant's real property data through this one route with no error and no test catching it. Handed to whoever owns smartcity-os next (not G-122, which this mission was told not to touch the auth middleware alongside); the fix shape would be replacing that literal with the same getBastropTenantId()-style name-based lookup the five mygov.ts platform routes already use, closing rule 2.4's own paired-implementation-drift pattern inside that one file.

A minor free finding (DEV_PROCESS 1.4, not investigated further, out of this mission's authorized touch surface): getBastropTenantId()'s own not-found fallback is hardcoded 1, while the separately-named DEFAULT_TENANT_ID constant used elsewhere in the same file is 2 -- two different literals for conceptually the same 'no real tenant resolved' case, in the same file, and they disagree.

defect3.enumerationOfPlatformRoutes: 12 GET routes across 7 files register requirePlatformInternalKey (grepped app.get(...requirePlatformInternalKey across server/routes/*.ts, confirmed no router-mounted /api/platform prefix exists elsewhere via a broader /api/platform text search across 8 files): firstdue.ts (apparatus), goto.ts (call-summary), mygov.ts x5 (permits, work-orders, inspections, code-violations, business-licenses), powerbi.ts (cip-projects), property-intelligence.ts x2 (summary, layers), samsara.ts (vehicles), spireon.ts (vehicles).
defect3.answer: PLATFORM_INTERNAL_API_KEY itself is bound to no tenant at all -- it is one global bearer secret gating all 12 routes uniformly (requirePlatformInternalKey is a pure token-equality check, and commit d2d3648 (#40, verified at source) added /platform to routes.ts's publicPrefixes allowlist specifically to bypass session/tenant-context middleware, relying on the key alone). Tenant resolution downstream of the key is a per-route implementation choice and is NOT uniform: (1) the 5 mygov.ts platform routes resolve Bastrop by a dynamic, name-based lookup -- getBastropTenantId(), `WHERE tenants.slug = 'bastrop'`, cached after first resolution, falling back to literal 1 only if no such row exists -- a genuine, intentional, non-accidental binding. (2) /api/platform/property-intel/summary resolves its tenant via the bare DEFAULT_TENANT_ID literal (=2), NOT looked up by name, and feeds a real SQL `WHERE tenant_id = $1` filter in getPropertySummary's three sub-queries (getPropertyPermits/getPropertyViolations/getPropertyInspections, server/services/property-intelligence.ts). This is exactly the accidental-default pattern the dispatch flagged: DEFAULT_TENANT_ID was flipped 1->2 in commit 0e5c41e (verified at source) for an unrelated reason (a manager-load roster fix touching three files: mygov.ts, job-queue.ts, property-intelligence.ts), and this route inherited that change incidentally. A second unrelated bump, or a tenant-id renumbering, would silently serve a different tenant's real property data through this one route, with no error and no test to catch it. (3) /api/platform/property-intel/layers uses no tenant id at all -- it queries a Bastrop-specific ArcGIS layer registry directly, single-city by construction. (4) The remaining 5 vendor-integration platform routes (samsara/spireon/firstdue/powerbi/goto) have no tenant concept whatsoever -- each is a direct read from this deployment's own single vendor account/credential (Samsara token, Spireon creds, etc.), correct by construction today because smartcity-os is presently one deployment for one city, not by any tenant-row scoping that could later diverge the way (2) already has once.
